good.text: In the absence of a social registry with sufficient coverage in urban and peri-urban areas, the RRR is being developed through two key innovations: (a) geographic targeting based on poverty maps—1,163 of the poorest urban wards with a total population of over 20 million people were selected based on the ward-level poverty maps produced by applying cutting-edge machine learning algorithms to granular satellite imagery data,27 and (b) mobile-based self-registration—potential beneficiaries in the selected wards were invited to self-register through an unstructured supplementary service data (USSD) application through targeted and localized short message service (SMS) blasts in the selected wards.

Progress includes adjustments to (Number) achieving targets homogeneous areas, methodological validation for estimating value per square meter, and technical coordination with MEF on machine learning models.
